name: Jackie Robinson
hook: The man who broke baseball's color line — No. 42, Branch Rickey, and the Dodgers.

facts.label: broke the color line
facts.statement: He broke baseball's color line in 1947 with the Brooklyn Dodgers after starring for the Kansas City Monarchs, and spent his whole major league career there.

facts.label: Branch Rickey
facts.statement: Dodgers owner Branch Rickey, nicknamed "Mahatma," signed him; Harrison Ford played Rickey to Chadwick Boseman's Robinson in the film 42.

facts.label: No. 42
facts.statement: His number 42 is retired throughout Major League Baseball, and the 2013 film about him used it as its title.

facts.label: the middle name Roosevelt
facts.statement: Born in January 1919, the month Theodore Roosevelt died, he was given the middle name Roosevelt.

facts.label: the 1947 Time cover
facts.statement: He appeared on the September 22, 1947, cover of Time, captioned "He and the boss took a chance."

facts.label: Spingarn Medal and Medal of Freedom
facts.statement: He won the NAACP's Spingarn Medal and, posthumously, the Presidential Medal of Freedom; Jesse Jackson delivered his 1972 eulogy.

facts.label: stealing home
facts.statement: He stole home in Game 1 of the 1955 World Series, one of the most dramatic plays in the sport.
